tiers.T1: A dedicated tool does the operation.
tiers.T2: Reachable through a generic tool, with a recipe that was run and checked.
tiers.T3: Documented. Not opened as a tool, or reachable only through a generic tool without a verified recipe.

reasons.chemscript.interop: SWIG and native interop plumbing; not part of the SDK's API and never exposed.
reasons.chemscript.collection: Generated collection wrapper; reached through the property of its owning type.
reasons.chemscript.unverified: Reachable through execute_chemscript_sdk; no recipe has been run for this member yet.
reasons.com.default: Type-level entry of the ChemDraw automation library.
reasons.com.unverified: Reachable through chemdraw_com_call; no recipe has been run for this member yet.
reasons.com.blocked: chemdraw_com_call refuses it (hidden member, user clipboard, printing, menu commands or other state outside the document).
reasons.com.control: Part of the embeddable ChemDraw ActiveX control; the automation object chemdraw_com_call drives does not expose it.
reasons.com.enum: Enumeration of constants used as arguments to COM members.
reasons.com.coclass: Class identifier that creates the interfaces listed beside it.
reasons.menu.default: Not opened. Windows can run a command only through IChemOfficeMenuItem.Execute, which needs a visible ChemDraw with the document active, and a command that opens a window can stop the session (Predict 1H-NMR Shifts did not return); chemdraw_com_call refuses the menu types. Where a COM member does the same work, as IChemDrawObjects.Clean does for Clean Up Structure, use that.
reasons.cdxml.default: Named in ChemDraw's own files but never seen in a document here; chemdraw_object accepts it, untested.
reasons.cdxml.object: chemdraw_object lists, reads, changes, adds and deletes it with catalog-checked attributes; the edit is structural, not a layout.
reasons.cdxml.unconfirmed: Name from the CDXML format with no evidence in this installation.

overrides.reason: Opens the source document for conversion.
